newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn issues 6.86 bln dmk of 10-yr bond at auction.
newsitem.headline: Bonn issues 6.86 bln dmk of 10-yr bond at auction.

text.p: The German government on Wednesday issued 6.86 billion marks of a new 10-year bond bearing a six percent coupon at auction at a lowest accepted price of 100.36, the Bundesbank as issuing agent said.
The average yield for the auction tranche was 5.94 percent.
A five billion-mark first tranche of the bond was issued to the Federal Bond Consortium on Tuesday.
The Bundesbank said it was retaining 3.14 billion marks of the issue for market-smoothing purposes, bringing the total volume of the issue to 15 billion marks.
The bond matures on January 4, 2007, and the first interest payment is due on January 4, 1998.
The Bundesbank has said a further 10 billion marks worth of the bond will be issued in the third 10 days of January.

The bond, the first federal 10-year bond issue since last April, will be listed on Monday, January 13 and is expected to be strippable from July 1997 onwards. Stripping a bond allows separate trading of its principal and coupon.
